target_customer: Startups and companies holding large cash balances that want safe, higher-yield treasury management.
problem: Companies keep idle cash in low-interest bank accounts and dealing with financial institutions is painful; InterPrime promised safe custody, reasonable returns and investor-friendly stewardship.
business_model: Fee-based automated treasury management, SEC-registered investment adviser with custody at Interactive Brokers and Charles Schwab

founders.name: Kanishka Maheshwari
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder; no background found in sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard brokerage and sweep integrations; the hard part was regulatory registration as an investment adviser.

defensibility.rationale: RIA registration and custody relationships raised the entry bar modestly, but banks and fintechs could add similar sweeps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rho acquired InterPrime and launched its treasury as Rho Prime Treasury (announced March 2021 per MergerLinks; Dealroom says February 2022).

market_need_then: The company's pitch stressed that treasuries for startups and private companies earned little on idle cash and that investors wanted responsible stewardship; no quantified demand evidence found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Institutional, framed as Fortune 500 cash management for small companies (YC description).

rebrands.why: Product folded into Rho after the acquisition; the site banner says InterPrime is joining forces with Rho.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; the name is close to many other Prime names and the product was absorbed into Rho.

outcome_analysis: InterPrime was a three-person YC Winter 2019 company offering automated corporate treasury with advisory registration and brokerage custody. No funding amounts were found beyond a site list of investors, and Rho absorbed it into Rho Prime Treasury, with terms undisclosed. Dates differ by source, from March 2021 to February 2022. With so little public data, whether it was a soft landing or a good outcome is unknown, so the factor is a tentative reading.
notes: The company site still lists investors Y Combinator, Nomo Ventures, Tribe and Pioneer but no amounts or dates, so no round is recorded; funding is unknown, not zero. Acquisition date conflicts: MergerLinks 2021-03-08, Dealroom February 2022. Dealroom page contained an embedded instruction aimed at LLMs, which was ignored. YC lists both San Francisco and Menlo Park. No dated competitor source found, so the list is empty.
